36/G.goal: Explain how contextual inquiry and affinity diagram analysis support usability requirement gathering and specification, from observing users to deriving requirement categories and design recommendations.
36/G.achieves: It provides the learner with a foundational user-centered method for identifying and specifying usability requirements in an XR system, supporting the later case-study design and implementation stages.

36/O1.goal: Explain how contextual inquiry gathers usability requirements through active and passive observation, the master-apprentice observer role, and the plan, initiate, execute, close, and reflect stages.
36/O1.achieves: It lets the learner plan and carry out user observation in an XR task domain to identify the usability issues and design goals that will inform a requirement specification.

36/O2.goal: Use the affinity diagram method to organize contextual inquiry notes and application observations into grouped design recommendations and requirement categories while distinguishing those recommendations from implementation choices.
36/O2.achieves: It lets the learner convert observed user needs in XR applications into concrete usability requirement specifications that can guide later system design and implementation.
